incbot: :rotating_light: Pager: p99 tail latency spike detected for streaming.generate in eu-west-2 starting ~4398765432. SLO breaches on p95/p99 for streaming sessions, increased error-rate for some clients. Auto-runbook recommended: collect tcpdumps, rollout routing failover if healthy.
oncall-evan: I'm on it. Looking at console now, seeing p99 jump to ~3.2s and several Streaming stalls flagged in traces.
sre-jen: copying perf dashboards — latency heatmap shows spikes across azb->azc cross-zone paths, retransmits & TLS handshake spikes. Packet loss counters trending up at the NAT tier.
net-eng-kumar: @oncall-evan @sre-jen seeing same — NAT ELB metrics show increased conntrack entries and SYN retransmits. Possible conntrack exhaustion + path reordering. Sending tcpdump snippet.
net-eng-kumar: ```
14:22:11.123456 IP 10.0.2.45.443 > 10.1.4.23.52344: Flags [S.], seq 1000, ack 2000, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 98765], length 0
14:22:11.223789 IP 10.0.2.45.443 > 10.1.4.23.52344: Flags [P.], seq 1001:1050, ack 2001, win 64240, length 49
... (retransmits, dup acks) ...
```
product-ara: Customer impact? Any user-visible errors or just slow streams? CS wants a canned line.
cs-lee: I'm seeing 12 customer reports in the inbox referencing 'stream freezing' and 'very long wait for first token' starting ~14:22 UTC. A few are high-tier. Need ETA for mitigation.
oncall-evan: Initial impact: elevated latency and some streaming stalls (clients see long gaps between chunks). Not universal — seems tied to requests routed through nat-pool-3 in eu-west-2b.
sre-jen: Correlating with deploys: none around window. BGP/ecmp path flaps none. Likely resource pressure at NAT gateway instances (conntrack saturation + queuing).
net-eng-kumar: Quick mitigation options: 1) Apply egress-steer to shift traffic away from nat-pool-3 to nat-pool-1/2 (fast). 2) Scale up NAT fleet in eu-west-2b (slower). 3) Flush conntrack entries on affected nodes (risky for active connections). Recommend #1 immediately and #2 as followup.
oncall-evan: Do #1 now. Prep runbook steps. Who can apply egress-steer?
net-eng-kumar: I can push egress-steer via infra control plane. Doing canary now for 10% traffic to nat-pool-1.
net-eng-kumar: `infractl route modify --region eu-west-2 --selector nat-pool=nat-pool-3 --weight 90 --towards nat-pool-1=10`
oncall-evan: :eyes: watching telemetry.
incbot: Alert: routing change deployed at 4398765460 by net-eng-kumar.
net-eng-kumar: Canary metrics look promising — retransmits down ~30% in the canary subset. Rolling to 50%.
sre-jen: Streaming stalls p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.8s in canary, overall p95 improved as well. Keep rolling.
product-ara: Notifying CS with interim update: "We're seeing elevated streaming latency in eu-west-2; mitigation in progress, switching traffic to alternate egress. We'll update in 15m."
cs-lee: sending update to affected customers now.
net-eng-kumar: Rolling to 100% egress-steer at 4398765483.
incbot: Routing change completed. Monitoring for regressions.
sre-jen: After full roll, packet loss counters normalized and TLS handshake times returned to baseline. p99 now ~700ms. Still above ideal but much better.
oncall-evan: Follow-ups: schedule NAT fleet scale-up and increase conntrack max on nodes by 20% to avoid recurrence. Also add alert for conntrack utilization.
net-eng-kumar: Agreed. I'll open infra ticket to scale nat-pool-3 to +2 instances and add sysctl change `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` bump test in staging.
product-ara: We should also add a routing failover play to the streaming runbook: prefer multi-nat pools and automated egress-steer when conntrack>80%.
sre-jen: Forensics: we saw sudden connection bursts from a small subset of clients opening many long-lived streams — contributed to conntrack pressure. Need to throttle long pollers or encourage multiplexing.
cs-lee: I'll reach out to those customers and suggest SDK updates to use connection reuse.
oncall-evan: Any customer facing error messages to send now? CS drafted: "We mitigated elevated streaming latency in eu-west-2 by rerouting traffic and are continuing to harden NAT capacity; no data loss reported." Approve?
product-ara: Approve. Add that engineers are monitoring and will follow up with root cause timeline.
net-eng-kumar: Opening post-incident ticket with logs, tcpdumps, and the routing change diff: https://infra.internal/tickets/INC-4398765432
sre-jen: Adding next-step action items: - scale NAT pool - add conntrack alert - add egress-steer automation - update streaming runbook - investigate client burst patterns
oncall-evan: Thanks team. Paging clear for now. Will keep watch for 1 hour and then hand to oncall rotation notes. :thumbsup:
incbot: Incident status update: mitigated — monitoring. Timestamp 4398765499."
